content.title: Austin Reaves projected return date revealed: Latest injury update
content.text: Austin Reaves is expected to return in roughly 4-6 weeks, though the minimum recovery time of a Grade 2 oblique strain is around 3 weeks and could extend to 5 if rib cartilage involvement is present. Los Angeles Lakers star guard Austin Reaves has been diagnosed with a Grade 2 oblique strain (partial tear) and is officially expected to miss at least the remainder of the regular season. Los Angeles Lakers / Schedule So when could he realistically return? According to sports doctor Evan Jeffries, the typical recovery timeline for this type of injury is around 4-6 weeks. That would likely keep Reaves out through the start of the playoffs, with the first round beginning on April 18. Injury specialist Jeff Stotts adds more context. Oblique strains are more common in MLB, with an average time lost of about 46 days. In the NBA, less severe or unspecified oblique injuries lead to an average absence of around 16.7 days, while high-grade tears can sideline players for roughly nine weeks. Reaves' return will likely fall somewhere in between those timelines. Credit ZUMAPRESS.com - Scanpix Doctor Jesse Morse emphasizes that these injuries are particularly painful because the nerves are close to the rib attachments. He also notes that rushing back too soon increases the risk of reinjury, similar to Luka Doncic and his current Grade 2 hamstring strain. The minimum recovery time is typically around three weeks, but it can extend closer to five if there's any rib cartilage involvement. Reaves suffered an oblique strain in the Lakers' 139-96 loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder last Thursday. Subscribe to BN+ and get access to exclusive content.
